**8B.5 Research Note**

Kishida shows **moderately strong internal follow-through in 2024**, especially on disaster response, budget execution, and passing legislation through the cabinet-Diet machinery. The main weakness is **party discipline and coordination inside the LDP**, where the funding scandal exposed persistent factional looseness and defensive crisis management.

**Positive**
- [Policy Speech by Prime Minister Kishida to the 213th Session of the Diet](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/30shiseihoshin.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-01-30 | Kishida set a concrete yearly agenda and tied it to execution through the Diet and cabinet, naming disaster response, wage growth, child support, fiscal reform, digital administration, labor reform, and defense buildup; this is direct evidence of cross-ministry coordination around a defined program. QIDs: 8B.5, 8B.2, 8B.3
- [Prime Minister Orders on Noto Earthquake Response](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/decisions/2024/0101shiji.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-01-01 | Kishida ordered timely warnings, evacuation, damage prevention, and emergency response with human life first, showing centralized crisis command over ministries and local authorities. QIDs: 8B.5, 8B.2
- [Press Conference by Prime Minister Kishida](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/11kaiken.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-01-11 | He explicitly ordered secondary evacuation for elderly people, infants, nursing mothers, disabled people, and others needing care, which shows follow-through into operational guidance for local implementation. QIDs: 8B.5, 8B.2
- [Press Conference by Prime Minister Kishida](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/25kaiken.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-01-25 | Kishida announced cash aid, housing support, and livelihood restoration for disaster victims, indicating the state machinery was being directed to deliver concrete assistance rather than merely issue statements. QIDs: 8B.5, 8B.2, 8B.3
- [Press Conference by Prime Minister Kishida](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202406/21kaiken.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-06-21 | Kishida said the revised Political Funds Control Act had been amended and a third-party inspections-and-audits body was the next step, evidence that he could push institutional follow-through even under scandal pressure. QIDs: 8B.5, 8B.3, 8B.4
- [Prime Minister’s Office statement on active cyber defense](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/actions/202406/07cyber.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-06-07 | Kishida convened a 17-expert panel and told ministers to turn its results into bills as early as possible, a direct example of coordinating experts, bureaucracy, and legislation. QIDs: 8B.5, 8B.3, 8B.4
- [Liaison Meeting of the Government and Ruling Parties](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/actions/202407/03sei_yoto.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-07-03 | Kishida said nearly all bills and treaties passed, including the Political Funds Control Act and child-care and agriculture measures, and credited the government-ruling-party coalition; this is strong evidence of legislative and party coordination. QIDs: 8B.5, 8B.2, 8B.3
- [Emergency disaster recovery update](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202407/01kaiken.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-07-01 | Kishida said more than 550 billion yen in reserve funds had been used in multiple tranches to restore infrastructure, lifelines, housing, and livelihoods, showing routinized follow-through across implementing agencies. QIDs: 8B.5, 8B.2

**Negative / Mixed**
- [Prosecutors indict several LDP faction members over funds scandal](https://english.kyodonews.net/news/2024/01/f4d6ea5b7d8f-update1-prosecutors-indict-several-ldp-faction-members-over-funds-scandal.html) | Kyodo News | 2024-01-19 | Prosecutors indicted figures in Kishida’s factional orbit over undisclosed revenue, showing that faction discipline and financial control inside the ruling party were weak rather than tightly commanded. QIDs: 8B.5, 8B.4, 8B.3
- [Kyodo: LDP agrees to amend rules to strengthen governance amid funds scandal](https://english.kyodonews.net/news/2024/03/62a74c2cb396-ldp-agrees-to-amend-rules-to-strengthen-governance-amid-funds-scandal.html?phrase=number+of+vaccinated&words=) | Kyodo News | 2024-03-07 | The party needed rule changes because factions had been used to secure funds and allocate key posts, which is direct evidence of weak internal discipline and persistent factional autonomy. QIDs: 8B.5, 8B.4, 8B.3
- [Embattled Japan PM faces ethics committee to save popularity and budget](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/embattled-japan-pm-faces-ethics-committee-to-save-popularity-and-budget-3319362) | Reuters | 2024-02-28 | Kishida’s appearance before the ethics committee shows his administration was pulled into defensive damage control, consuming bandwidth that otherwise would have gone to disciplined execution. QIDs: 8B.5, 8B.4
- [Japan’s lower house passes budget in win for PM Kishida](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/japans-lower-house-passes-budget-in-win-for-pm-kishida-3319362) | Reuters | 2024-03-02 | The budget passed, but Reuters framed it as a win for a leader with slumping support, suggesting formal coordination still depended on fragile political capital rather than robust party discipline. QIDs: 8B.5, 8B.3
- [Japan PM Kishida won’t run for reelection at LDP race](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/japan-pm-kishida-wont-run-for-reelection-at-ldp-race-3570455) | Reuters | 2024-08-14 | Reuters said scandals and rising living costs eroded support and Kishida stepped aside to show the LDP was changing, which is mixed evidence: he accepted succession, but the need for a reset shows weakened internal control. QIDs: 8B.5, 8B.4, 8B.3
- [Kishida compromised with conservative nationalists to stay in power](https://apnews.com/article/05926b50f4f5a83a631f779d906cf06d) | Associated Press | 2024-09-30 | AP described Kishida as compromising with conservative nationalists and operating inside a faction-driven party system, which suggests coalition management and internal bargaining were as important as top-down discipline. QIDs: 8B.5, 8B.4, 8B.3
- [Freedom House: Japan 2024](https://freedomhouse.org/country/japan/freedom-world/2024) | Freedom House | 2024 | Freedom House flags close government-business relations, factional politics, and institutional frictions, which supports a structural reading that Kishida did not fully tame elite networks or internal veto players. QIDs: 8B.5, 8B.4, 8B.3

**Search Gap**
- I found strong evidence for execution through disaster response, budgeting, and legislation, but **little direct evidence on regional governors, territorial administration, or security-force command failures/successes** in 2024.
- The clearest negative evidence is **party discipline**, not territorial or coercive-state discipline. The record does not show open defiance by ministries or security forces, but it also does not show a tightly unified ruling machine.
